thread:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] p99 latency crossed SLO (api-prod /v1/generate) — region us-west-2. Alert started ~2026-03-12T02:34:56Z. paging: on-call

Alice Chen: seeing big tail spikes in streaming p99 across multiple shards, also a rise in streaming stalls reported by clients. p95 up ~2.5x, p99 > 3s on some traces.

Priya Nair: noticed KV cache eviction_count jump at 02:33. TTL evictions low but eviction_by_size high. Shard-level slab utilization uneven.

Marco Silva: loading recent metrics, stack: kv-cache (sharded C++ service) -> runtime decode -> networking. Looks like some slabs are full and others underutilized — fragmentation.

Lina Gomez: customers affected: several heavy streaming users (cs-ticket 3821, 3822). CS notified, asked for ETA and mitigation notes.

Jake Park: grabbing debug from node-13: 
```json
{"shard":"s-13","eviction_by_size":3421,"alloc_fail":23,"prefetch_hits":12,"decode_hits":1450}
```
prefetch_hits low vs decode_hits high — suggests prefetch/rehydration lagging.

Alice Chen: hypothesize imbalance: prefetch (we call "prefill" internally) workers falling behind decode path -> clients get misses -> decode path does synchronous load-> high tail latency and stalls because load thundering rebuilds cache.

Marco Silva: quick mitigation proposals (in order):
1) Reduce prefetch concurrency on cluster to smooth background load (kv.config.prefetch_concurrency=4 -> 2)
2) Enable temporary slab-growth on impacted shards: kv.admin.slab_resize(+20%) for s-13,s-14
3) Route critical streaming traffic to fallback model variant with smaller KV footprint (model-x-small) for next 30m
4) Roll a small canary patch to increase decode worker pool timeouts to prevent blocking streaming threads

Priya Nair: I'll run slab resize for s-13 and s-14 first, low-risk. Doing now.

deploy-bot: accepted command from Priya Nair: `kvctl slab-resize --shards s-13,s-14 --delta 20%`

Priya Nair: slab resize returned ok on s-13, s-14. Watching metrics.

Alice Chen: Marco, can you throttle prefetch? Which flag?

Marco Silva: patching kv config on config service: `kv.runtime.prefetch_work_concurrency=2` then rollout to us-west-2. Doing a canary (10% nodes) first.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: kv-config-v2026-03-12-pt1 -> 10% nodes (us-west-2)

(10m pass)
Marco Silva: canary pass looks good, prefetch queue length dropped 80% on canary nodes, p99 on those nodes fell from ~2.8s -> ~600ms. Rolling to remaining nodes now.

Alice Chen: good. Observed streaming stalls decreasing overall but still seeing occasional >2s tails on older shards. Priya, how's slab imbalance after resize?

Priya Nair: slab utilization evening out on s-13/s-14; eviction_by_size rate down 40%. Still seeing one shard s-08 with high alloc_fail. Scheduling s-08 for resize next.

Lina Gomez: note for CS: initial mitigation (throttle prefetch + slab resize) applied, customer-facing impact reduced; recommend telling customers we implemented temporary routing and are monitoring.

Jake Park: adding temporary routing rule now: `route-config add --match "customer in (enterprise-streamers)" --to model-x-small --duration 30m`

deploy-bot: routing rule activated (id: r-7783).

incident-bot: Severity update -> degraded (was partial outage). p99 still above target but trending down.

Marco Silva: handing off to Marco Silva for overnight watch. Summary for next on-call: 1) prefetch concurrency reduced; 2) resized slabs s-13,s-14; 3) routing rule in place for high-volume streamers; 4) s-08 queued for resize; 5) follow up: schedule a controlled compaction step to reduce fragmentation.

Alice Chen: quick customer impact numbers: approx 12 tenant streams saw >1.5s stalls during peak window (02:32-02:50 UTC). No data loss; only increased latency and occasional stream resets.

Lina Gomez: CS updated customers 3821/3822 with mitigation notes, offered a post-incident write-up.

Marco Silva: leaving a short runbook items in #eng-sre/incident-ops: "If p99 jumps >2s again: 1) prefetch throttle -> 1; 2) enable per-shard slab autoscale; 3) temporarily route high-volume streams to model-x-small."

Jake Park: paging status -> resolved alert cleared at 02:48 for canary, global cleared at 03:02 but monitor for regressions for 24h.

pagerduty: PagerDuty note: incident acknowledged by Alice Chen at 02:36, resolved by Marco Silva at 03:02.

Priya Nair: scheduling deeper investigation tomorrow: collect heap snapshots, slab allocation histograms, and run compaction job on a staging cluster to validate.

Alice Chen: thanks team. Handing off to Marco for follow-up and postmortem. If anything spikes again ping with @here and re-escalate to infra. :thumbsup:
